name: kb_bible_commit
description: Commit one round of confirmed entries to the bible: { ids, baseBranch, baseCommit, demoted_ids?, withdrawals?, restore_ids? }. Merges exactly the given ids from this repository's KB into <repo>/.fleet/kb-canonical.json at ENTRY level -- only the given ids are added or replaced; every entry already in the file is kept unless this KB holds it as superseded or invalidated, and an entry in the file but not in the KB (or CONFIRMED and current, or merely stale) is never dropped -- in kb_export's stable serialization (v3 envelope, id order, ASCII-safe; each merged entry carries its stored source_file_hashes basis). provenance.branch is baseBranch (the sprint's target base branch) and provenance.commit is baseCommit (the base commit the entries were verified against), never the working folder HEAD. Then makes a local commit scoped to that one path (identity pm-kb). It NEVER pushes. Re-running with the same ids after resetting to a newer HEAD re-merges at entry level, so a rejected push can be retried with no manual merge. Ids that are unknown, stale, superseded, or not CONFIRMED are SKIPPED (never an error) and reported in skipped with reason not_confirmed_or_unknown. A CONFIRMED id is admitted only if it passes the same basis rule kb_export (scope=project) applies: every cited source file has a recorded per-file hash that matches that file's content at the repo's HEAD commit (an empty or missing basis, a cited file with no basis key, a file absent or changed at HEAD, or a path that is not repo-relative excludes it; uncommitted edits never change the verdict; a folder that is not a git work tree is refused, never hashed from disk); such an id is SKIPPED with reason basis_mismatch, logged, and any entry already in the bible for it is left unchanged. A CONFIRMED id that cites no source file has no checkable basis and is SKIPPED with its own reason no_source_files (never basis_mismatch), also leaving any existing bible entry unchanged. demoted_ids (optional) records DEMOTIONS EXPLICITLY: each id must name a local entry that carries a demoted_at and is now below CONFIRMED (i.e. kb_demote ran on it); any other id -- unknown, never demoted, or since re-promoted to CONFIRMED -- is SKIPPED with reason not_demoted_or_unknown and nothing changes for it. An admitted id is REMOVED from entries and upserted into the bible's OPTIONAL top-level demotions array as a tombstone {id, at, reason} carrying the LOCAL row's demoted_at as at and reason "demoted" (and does the same, every call, for each bible entry this KB holds as demoted, unless that entry was promoted after the local demotion), so another clone applies the demotion explicitly instead of inferring it from an absence (a clone legitimately holds CONFIRMED entries that were never exported). A demoted tombstone is written only for an id the bible at baseCommit carries (as an entry or a tombstone): a locally demoted entry this branch added (absent from the base) is removed from entries with no tombstone, any other demoted_ids id is SKIPPED with reason not_in_base_bible, and when baseCommit does not resolve or its bible is unreadable no new demoted tombstone is written (such demoted_ids ids are skipped not_in_base_bible, and the result carries base_bible_error naming the read failure) while tombstones already in the file are kept. Tombstones already in the file are PRESERVED by a later commit carrying unrelated ids, and re-committing a demoted-tombstoned id through ids after a re-promotion restores its entry and CLEARS its tombstone. A WITHDRAWN tombstone in the current file (branch-added or merged from the base) is never cleared by ids: such an id is SKIPPED with reason withdrawn_tombstone and its tombstone kept, unless restore_ids undoes that (branch-added) tombstone in the same call. A withdrawn tombstone also outranks a demotion: a demoted_ids id the current file carries a withdrawn tombstone for is SKIPPED with reason withdrawn_tombstone, the every-call demotion rule passes over it, and a demoted tombstone never replaces a withdrawn one (so a later ids re-promotion cannot clear the withdrawal). A demoted tombstone in the current file blocks an ids merge unless the id's local trust time is strictly after the tombstone at (a real re-promotion, which clears the tombstone); otherwise the id is SKIPPED with reason demoted_tombstone and the tombstone kept. An id found in both entries and demotions on any call loses its entry (the tombstone wins) and is reported in removed with reason tombstoned. provenance.entry_count counts entries only -- a tombstone is not an entry. At every call (also with no ids) each bible entry this KB holds as superseded or invalidated is REMOVED and reported in removed as {id, reason} (reason superseded or invalidated); the commit message lists each removal. kb_export never removes entries. Also at every call, each bible entry with no source_file_hashes (carried over from a v1/v2 bible) that this KB holds under the same id, citing the same source files, with a stored basis that passes the same basis rule at HEAD gains that stored basis as its source_file_hashes (only that field changes; an entry that does not qualify is kept unchanged, never dropped); backfilled reports how many, and the commit message names the count. Nothing merged, nothing removed, nothing demotable and nothing backfilled, or an unchanged entry and tombstone set: no write and no commit. Refuses (throws, file untouched) when the existing bible file is unreadable or holds a duplicate id, or when the local commit fails. withdrawals (optional, [{id, note, evidence_files}]) records WITHDRAWALS carried by this branch: an id the bible holds as an entry, or this KB holds CONFIRMED (not superseded, not a user-directive), is REMOVED from entries and recorded as a tombstone {id, at: now, reason: "withdrawn", note, evidence_files}; the local entry is NOT changed -- other clones apply it only on a kb_import of the merged base bible. Any other id, or one also merged or demoted in the same call, is SKIPPED with reason not_withdrawable. restore_ids (optional) undoes tombstones this branch added: one is removed only when the bible at baseCommit carries none for the id, and the base bible's entry for it is re-added byte-identical. Under an http KB provider entry merging is skipped with bible_skipped:true and a reason, never an error (the KB is not read); with no withdrawals and no restore_ids nothing is written or committed, with them only the tombstones are written (a tombstone-only bible is created when absent) and committed. Returns {path, merged, demoted, withdrawn, restored, skipped, removed, entry_count, backfilled, committed, base_bible_error?}; base_bible_error is present only when a rule needed the bible at baseCommit (a demotion gate or a restore) and it could not be read (baseCommit does not resolve, or its bible does not parse) -- the call still fails closed. Scope: always the calling session's own KB -- a member session uses its registered work folder; any other session uses the first MCP client root (roots/list) inside a git repository with an origin remote, as that repository's top level, or the fleet server's working folder when the client offers no roots; there is no repo/path scope argument (the removed repo_path, repo and repo_remote_url keys fail with E-SCOPE-KEY-REMOVED). Fails with E-SELF-NO-WORKFOLDER, E-SELF-NOT-A-REPO or E-SELF-NO-REMOTE (each with a one-line remediation) when that folder cannot carry a KB identity (it must be a git repository with an origin remote).
